title: PROOF-OF-SPEC deliverable (Andrew-direct 2026-08-11 ~0815Z): the machine-readable completion contract every Tier-2 build TO assignee fills to prove work was done TO SPEC. A TO without a schema-valid instance is NOT complete.
description: GENRE (2026-10-04, 1.0.0_SA_CTO~Z on the 3.0.0_SA_CVO verdict msg 29306): an instance is genre BUILD (root `genre` absent or BUILD) or genre DEPLOY. BUILD validates exactly as before the split: the `else` branch carries the {mutant, determinism} controls block and the closed key set that sat at the root, both unchanged. DEPLOY (`then`) proves a redeploy, which has no mutant: its `controls` are NAMED controls, each a read with one expected value when the act landed and another when it did not, and it requires never_widen_pair, risk_class and a named rollback. proof-of-spec-check.py adds what draft-07 cannot carry: DEPLOY is admitted only when the governing order carries the issuer's line-anchored <proof_genre>DEPLOY</proof_genre> beside <risk>SERVED</risk> or <risk>WORLD</risk>; at least one control must DISCRIMINATE (status PASS and expected_landed != expected_not_landed); any DID-NOT-DISCRIMINATE control makes the instance INVALID; rollback must be non-empty. The common properties and the 12 required keys stay at the root, so the checker's no-jsonschema fallback still reads them there.

genre.description: OPTIONAL; absent means BUILD, so every instance written before 2026-10-04 is BUILD and validates as it did. DEPLOY is a CLAIM the checker grades against the governing order's issuer mark (<proof_genre>DEPLOY</proof_genre> with <risk>SERVED|WORLD</risk>); the graded party cannot confer it on itself, or a build order would escape its mutant.

firm.description: OPTIONAL, additive (ratified with TIGHTENING J1, CTO G-C @42317a4aab): the firm this instance proves work for, stated exactly instead of derived from to_id grammar. The proof-board (to-check.py --proof-board) prefers this field; absent it, the DECLARED derivation is leading to_id token in this same enum, else UNPARSED -- never guessed. Existing instances without it remain valid. FABRIC added 2026-08-19 (CTO, on 0.8.0's Rule-24 exhaustiveness finding 220017Z): fabric-infrastructure work (D0-class -- broker, comp-tools, gates) proves work for NO client firm, and the J1 declare-on-next-touch instruction was unsatisfiable without a value for it -- an inexhaustive enum on a ratified schema forces either a false firm or a permanent violation.

decomp_ref.description: The L7 completion gate of the canonical fabric workflow (org/ref/CANONICAL_FABRIC_WORKFLOW_20260901.md; build routed to the tooling lane on Andrew's word in the ratification). OPTIONAL AT THE SCHEMA LEVEL, CONDITIONALLY REQUIRED BY THE CHECKER: proof-of-spec-check.py requires this object when, and only when, the instance's project is dep_stage-REGISTERED (a dep_stage key present in org/projects/{CODE}.json -- 10 of 326 projects on 2026-08-24). It is optional here so the 126 of 131 existing instances belonging to non-pipeline projects remain schema-valid; making it a root-level required key would invalidate them wholesale for a rule that does not bind them. WHY THE FIELD HAD TO BE ADDED AT ALL: this schema's root is additionalProperties:false, so before this there was NO SLOT for a decomp_ref, and the estate had already routed around the gap -- ETFS_POSITIONING.TO-2's delivered instance carries its decomp_ref as PROSE inside spec_ref.doc. That is the schema forcing a free-text workaround, not an assignee defect, and free text cannot be joined against a decomp.

doc.description: path to the stage-3 decomp run artifact this work discharges, e.g. workflows/atom_decomposition/runs/etfs-positioning/20260821T194927Z/DECOMP.md

vintage_commit.description: the decomp vintage built against. Same discipline as spec_ref.vintage_commit: a citation without a vintage is not a citation -- a decomp path alone resolves at every vintage, to different cells.

to_ref.description: path to the TO file whose ISSUANCE half carries the machine-readable <criterion id=.. cell_refs=../> declarations and the <decomp_ref> declared cell set. STATED, NEVER DERIVED FROM to_id BY FILENAME: Rule 22a's build-input rule -- a filename-resolved lookup reports drift where there is none and reads clean where two copies have diverged. The bidirectional alignment check is a JOIN against this file; cell_refs are read as DECLARED and are never inferred, because a retrofitted derivation makes alignment LOOK satisfied while being FALSE.

phase.description: What this proof's TO was: a phase of the DS-PIPELINE build program (P1..P5), ANY OTHER BUILD (BUILD-GENERAL -- component/tool/schema/gate builds outside that program), or the two non-build values. Rule-24: investigations and other non-build TOs prove to spec too, on their own axis value -- never shoehorned into a build phase. ADDED 2026-08-21 (BUILD-GENERAL, 2.0.0_SA_COO): the enum FAILED the CE half of postulate (i) against its own declared layer -- the five build members are the DS-pipeline program's phases ONLY, so every NON-DS build had no member and C6-KERNEL was FORCED to label itself NON-BUILD-OTHER, which is FALSE of a build. A NON-DS BUILD IS NEVER NON-BUILD-OTHER. Token chosen by census: the recommended 'BUILD-OTHER' is word-boundary-matched INSIDE its own sibling 'NON-BUILD-OTHER' (raw census 59 = 58 siblings + 1 real), so the two values would have been mutually unsearchable forever; BUILD-GENERAL is clean against all siblings at 0 prior occupancy. KNOWN RESIDUAL, DECLARED NOT HIDDEN: this axis carries TWO INTENTS -- which-phase-of-one-named-program x what-kind-of-work -- and therefore two grains, so it does not satisfy postulates (ii)/(iii); that defect PRE-EXISTS this member and is made visible by it, not caused by it. The Rule-24-correct remedy is a two-field split (work_kind x program_phase), DEFERRED under YAGNI per 4.0.0_SA_CRO until a consumer branches on the value -- none does today (proof-of-spec-check.py never reads phase; verified 0 mentions). Forward-only: committed instances are NOT relabelled (vintage law).

vintage_commit.description: the spec vintage built against -- a citation without a vintage is not a citation

kind.description: artifact KIND, one grain (Rule-24 collectively-exhaustive). frontend_component ADDED 2026-08-11 (COO 215014Z, routed): a portal/frontend code artifact -- WITHOUT it a portal component mis-declares as 'script' and gets scanned by the backend DS-id-grammar coverage heuristic it cannot satisfy. The artifact-coverage heuristic is backend-script-specific and scopes to (script, s3_object) BY DESIGN; frontend_component is outside it (a frontend-appropriate coverage rule is a follow-on gate candidate, not the enum's defect). ddb_rows ADDED 2026-10-09 (1.0.0_SA_CTO rule-24 ruling, row MDPF_SECCLASS-D1-S20): rows a deploy-genre act wrote to a DynamoDB table; path_or_key = dynamodb://<region>/<table> plus the key list or key-set file; commit_or_etag = the snapshot or read-back record, never a git pin; resolution skips it like s3_object. aws_resource ADDED 2026-10-09 (1.0.0_SA_CTO, row IRPT_DASHBD-S41): a live AWS resource that is neither an S3 object nor DynamoDB rows (e.g. a Secrets Manager secret, an IAM role, an SSM parameter); path_or_key is its ARN, commit_or_etag its version id; like s3_object and ddb_rows it is not a git ref, so resolution skips it and the order's own read-back holds the truth. Exclusive by construction: a resource that is an S3 object or DDB rows takes that kind.

deployed_state.description: an atomic commit is NOT an atomic deploy; state which

deploy_evidence.description: for DEPLOYED-VERIFIED: the live read proving it (ETag match / get-role-policy / describe). For other states: the reason.

introduces.description: OPTIONAL, additive (added 2026-08-30 by 1.0.0_SA_CTO~X on 1.0.0_SA_CTO 88109): the literal token(s) this artifact row INTRODUCES at its pin -- e.g. a call the fix adds. The checker requires every token PRESENT in the blob at commit_or_etag and ABSENT at the pin's parent (<pin>~1), or the file absent at the parent; a PENDING row is checked worktree-vs-HEAD. Without it a row is PRESENCE-resolved only (the pin exists and carries the path); with it the row is CONTENT-resolved (the pin carries the change). Class: a fix row pinned to an unrelated real commit resolved by presence (INDEXBYTES, 31579e177b). LIMIT: this proves the token MOVED between <pin>~1 and <pin>; it does NOT prove the token means what the citing face assumes -- it catches a stale pin, never a pin cited for the wrong reason (0.4.0_DS_ClientPlatform~V via 2.0.0_SA_COO 88511).

artifact_covered_by.description: OPTIONAL, additive (added 2026-08-19 by 0.8.0_AE_CloudComp per COO + DS base recommendation, instrument-repair batch): the criterion_id(s) whose rows cover this artifact, stated EXPLICITLY instead of inferred from the id grammar. The artifact-coverage rule previously keyed ONLY on the DS {firm}-{group}-{artifact}-{check} grammar, so a TO whose issuer minted ids in another grammar (WP1-N, D1b-N, D3.1-N) could not pass coverage no matter how complete the work was -- and the only available escape was declaring the CENTRAL DELIVERABLE 'excluded', i.e. a false statement. A rule whose sole route to green is a lie is not enforcing anything. Every id named here MUST exist in this instance's acceptance rows; a citation to a row that is not there is worse than no citation and is a violation. Existing instances without this field remain valid -- the checker now also accepts an artifact referenced by a row's invocation or output_evidence, which is COVERAGE evidence rather than NAMING evidence.

acceptance.description: ONE ROW PER CRITERION in the governing spec's acceptance battery. NO BARE VALUES: a PASS row with empty output_evidence INVALIDATES the whole deliverable.

criterion_verbatim.description: the spec's own words -- the assignee proves against the SPEC, not a paraphrase

invocation.description: the exact command/test run -- re-runnable by a verifier

output_evidence.description: verbatim output excerpt carrying the deciding values

denominator.description: every count states what it is out of; 'N/A' only with a reason, e.g. 'N/A -- boolean check'

status.description: UNCOMPUTABLE split 2026-08-11 (Rule-24 state coherence, CVO): -BY-CONSTRUCTION rides a NAMED later run (status_reason names it); UNVERIFIABLE-BY-INSTRUMENT names the SUBSTITUTE oracle in status_reason. Bare UNCOMPUTABLE is LEGACY (pre-split instances only) -- do not mint new

status_reason.description: REQUIRED (enforced by validator) when status != PASS; for UNCOMPUTABLE-BY-CONSTRUCTION it names the later run, for UNVERIFIABLE-BY-INSTRUMENT the substitute oracle

expect.description: spine v3.0 L6/L7 (one clause per criterion): the PATTERN (Python regex, searched with DOTALL) the deciding output must match; the checker grades a mechanical criterion by this match, not by the worker. Carried from the task order's <expect>. OPTIONAL: an instance without it is graded as before (self-report), which is the pre-v3 state and is stated as such.

judgment.description: spine v3.0 L6/L9: true marks a criterion the task order could not reduce to an invocation and an expectation. A judgment row carries its output and NO verdict -- status PASS or FAIL is REFUSED by the checker; use UNVERIFIABLE-BY-INSTRUMENT with status_reason naming the CVO at L9 as the oracle. The grade lands in the CVO's adjudication row (annex 4a).

controls.description: GENRE-DEPENDENT; the shape lives in the branches below -- BUILD (`else`): {mutant, determinism}, unchanged; DEPLOY (`then`): named discriminating controls. Nothing is constrained here, so no BUILD error is reported twice.

declared_exclusions.description: everything in scope NOT done, each with a reason -- an unmarked gap reads as coverage

surprises.description: surprise-channel entries: one line each, observed outside mandate, NO action taken. FORM (2026-09-03, Andrew-direct at the 3.0.0_SA_CVO terminal, relayed 92976; landed by 1.0.0_SA_CTO): each entry OPENS WITH THE ROW ID of the surprise as filed in the project's channel -- '<PROJECT>-S<n>: <one line>' (site Z: '<PROJECT>-Z-S<n>') -- because a surprise exists as a ROW (tree: org/missions/D*/<MACRO>/<CODE>/surprise-channel/investigations/INVESTIGATION_v{N}.md; flat: org/surprise_channel/<CODE>/) or it does not exist; a broker message is never the carrier. proof-of-spec-check.py's SURPRISES LIMB resolves the id on both roots and REFUSES the instance (hence the complete flip, via to-pipeline-gate check_complete_flip) when the governing TO is a TREE task order; flat-root and unresolved TOs get an ANNOUNCE frame only. The items stay `string` here deliberately: a pattern on this ratified schema would invalidate the 288 legacy instances wholesale for a rule that binds prospectively; the checker is the enforcer, this text is the carrier of the form.

session_log.description: path to the committed session log

then.description: genre DEPLOY: a redeploy's completion contract. Closed key set: the common keys, the deploy keys, and the deploy convention's carried fields (scope, status, carries, go_message, regression_reads, cold_reads, forward_notes; types from a census of the 23 AE deploy instances, 2026-10-04). A key outside this set is refused, as at BUILD.

controls.description: NAMED controls, {<name>: control}. A mutant has no meaning for a redeploy; the mutant's JOB survives as DISCRIMINATION: a read whose expected value differs between landed and not landed (a digest before/after, or a positive control). The checker requires at least one control with status PASS and expected_landed != expected_not_landed, and refuses the instance if any control reads DID-NOT-DISCRIMINATE.

expected_landed.description: the value this read returns when the act LANDED

expected_not_landed.description: the value this read returns when the act did NOT land; equal to expected_landed means the read cannot discriminate

status.description: DID-NOT-DISCRIMINATE: the read returned a value that does not separate landed from not landed; the deliverable is INVALID by its own control

never_widen_pair.description: the never-widen sign-off pair the act ran under (CLAUDE.md HARD STOPS), each half as path@commit; further per-leg keys are admitted

risk_class.description: the governing order's <risk> class; a LOCAL act is not a deploy

rollback.description: the NAMED rollback: the act that restores the prior state (e.g. the prior artifact version through one code-only safe-apply) and what triggers it

else.description: genre BUILD (root `genre` absent or BUILD): exactly the closed key set and the controls block that sat at the root before 2026-10-04.

controls.description: a passing assertion never mutated has never been tested

method.description: two same-input runs compared, or reason N/A
